title: LS2b: the auto-handover section ends at an explicit marker and renders titles on one line, so an embedded heading cannot split it
spec:
Bug in LS2 (on goal/T-1590): handover.write() ends the old section at the next line starting with '## ' (orchestrator/handover.py ~line 301). But _render_section embeds task and goal titles verbatim (`### {goal['id']} {goal['title']}` in _goal_lines ~line 109, and _task_ref), and goal T-1391's title contains '\n\n## Evidence\n...'. The section is then cut at that embedded heading; the rest of the old render is kept as 'tail' and the new render is written before it, so plan.md grows by one copy on every write.

Fix both sides:
1. Rendering: every title rendered into the section (goal headings in _goal_lines, refs from _task_ref, anything else that interpolates a title) is collapsed to one line: whitespace runs including newlines become a single space. No rendered line inside the section may start with '## ' except the section heading itself.
2. Boundary: _render_section ends the section with the line `<!-- end auto-handover -->`. write() takes the old section as running from the last '## Auto-handover ' heading through that marker line (inclusive) when the marker follows the heading; the tail is what follows the marker. When the marker is absent (a section written by older code), the old section runs to EOF (the pre-LS2 behaviour), so the first write after upgrade cleans up a legacy section. Remove the next-'## '-heading rule.
Keep: last-heading rule, temp-file plus os.replace write, snapshot-hash short-circuit, section == old_section no-op.
acceptance:

tests/test_handover.py::test_write_keeps_sections_after_handover and tests/test_handover.py::test_write_twice_stays_idempotent_with_tail still pass (update their fixtures to the marker form if needed)
